title: Kölnische Dramaturgie

description.main: Christopher Williams's book on Kochgeschirr Adapted for Use, his 2019 presentation at Frieze New York, which restaged his play Stage Play inside a gallery booth. It pairs black-and-white product shots from his Adapted for Use series with pictures of earlier art fairs and includes an essay by Tom McDonough.
description.extended:
Kölnische Dramaturgie documents Christopher Williams's 2019 presentation at Frieze New York, where he used an art fair booth as a stage set.

The presentation, Kochgeschirr Adapted for Use, restaged his 2017 theater production Stage Play. It added five new photographs, two silkscreen posters, a modular wall, and furniture designed by Franz West and Hans Accola. The photographs served as playscripts and the gallery's sales team as a theater troupe. The book takes Art Cologne 1967 as its reference. It pairs Williams's black-and-white product shots from the Adapted for Use series with pictures of earlier art fairs, among them a David Zwirner booth showing his own work. Petra Hollenbach designed the 50-page softcover, which carries a newly commissioned essay by the art historian Tom McDonough.

Williams was born in Los Angeles in 1956, studied at the California Institute of the Arts, and has been a professor at the Kunstakademie Düsseldorf since 2008. He lives and works in Cologne, Chicago, and Los Angeles, and David Zwirner has represented him since 2000. The book extends the Stage Play cycle, which Walther König published as a four-volume set in 2021.

notes: Year: Zwirner, Capitain Petzel and D.A.P. (pub date 1/9/2024) give 2024; DNB and Getty catalogue it as [2023]/©2023. Pages: 50 per Zwirner/CP/D.A.P.; DNB and Getty count 49. Dimensions: CP 21 × 22.9 cm, D.A.P. 8.25 × 9 in; Getty records 23 × 21 cm. Cover is the twelvebooks photograph of the printed book (uppercase title typography); the Zwirner/Capitain Petzel image is a pre-production render with different lettering, so it was not used. Designer Petra Hollenbach per Capitain Petzel. Subject headings are Getty's, not LOC's.
